stem.text: Fig. 6.1 is a diagram of part of a mitochondrion.

stem.caption: Fig. 6.1
stem.alt: Diagram of part of a mitochondrion: the outer mitochondrial membrane is a wavy double line at the top labelled 'cytoplasm' above it, with repeated protein structures embedded in it (one labelled 'protein'). Below, across the intermembrane space, the inner mitochondrial membrane is a second wavy double line labelled 'mitochondrial matrix' below it, with repeating sets of four embedded proteins labelled A, B, C and D.

stem.text: On Fig. 6.1, use arrows to show the route taken by oxygen from the cytoplasm into the mitochondrial matrix.

guidance: R arrows through proteins or A, B, C or D

points.text: an arrow through phospholipid layer in outer membrane and an arrow through phospholipid layer in inner membrane ;

explanation.text: Oxygen is a small non-polar molecule, so it passes straight through the phospholipid bilayer of each membrane by simple diffusion, not through any of the membrane proteins. The correct answer draws one arrow crossing the phospholipid part of the outer membrane and a second arrow crossing the phospholipid part of the inner membrane.

reasoningChain: Oxygen diffuses directly through the lipid part of a membrane because it is small and non-polar.
It must cross two membranes (outer, then inner) to reach the matrix, so draw one arrow through each phospholipid layer.

inferredMistakes.text: Drawing the arrow through one of the labelled proteins (A-D) or through the outer-membrane protein, rather than through the phospholipid bilayer itself; oxygen does not need a channel or carrier protein to cross a membrane.

stem.text: Identify protein D and the group of proteins represented by A, B and C and describe their roles in oxidative phosphorylation.

points.text: D = ATP synthase / ATP synthetase ; R ATPase
A, B and C = ETC / electron transport chain / electron carriers / electron acceptors ;
points.note: then any five from the list below, split into 'role of ETC proteins / A, B and C' and 'role of D'
role of ETC proteins / A, B and C

points.text: (use energy released) to pump / actively transport, H+ / protons, into intermembrane space ;
increases concentration of H+ / protons (in intermembrane space) / creates proton gradient ;
H+ / protons, diffuse through, ATP synthase / D ;
synthesis of ATP from ADP and Pi ;

markScheme.note: MS gives 2 compulsory identification marks (points 1-2) plus any 5 of the remaining 8 description points (points 3-10), for 7 marks total.

explanation.text: D is ATP synthase. A, B and C are the proteins of the electron transport chain (ETC) — electron carriers/acceptors embedded in the inner membrane.

Electrons are passed along the ETC (through A, B and C), releasing energy at each step. This energy is used to actively pump protons (H+) from the matrix into the intermembrane space, building up a high proton concentration there (a proton gradient).

Protons then diffuse back down this gradient, through ATP synthase (D), from the intermembrane space into the matrix. This flow of protons through ATP synthase drives the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate (Pi) — the whole process is called chemiosmosis.

reasoningChain: Name D (ATP synthase) and A/B/C (the electron transport chain).
Describe the ETC's role: electrons move along it, releasing energy used to pump protons into the intermembrane space.
Describe ATP synthase's role: protons diffuse back through it into the matrix, driving ATP synthesis from ADP + Pi.

inferredMistakes.text: Calling D 'ATPase' instead of 'ATP synthase'; the MS explicitly rejects ATPase because it implies breaking down ATP rather than making it.
Describing only one half of the process (either the ETC pumping protons, or ATP synthase making ATP) without linking them via the proton gradient, missing several of the available marks.

stem.text: The matrix of a mitochondrion contains small circular DNA. In the cells of humans, the mitochondria have circular DNA that contains 37 genes.
Suggest functions for these mitochondrial genes.

points.text: (named) enzyme for, Krebs cycle / link reaction ;
ETC proteins / cytochromes / electron carriers / electron acceptors / A / B / C ;
membrane / channel / transport / carrier / structural, proteins ;

explanation.text: Mitochondrial genes mostly code for proteins the mitochondrion itself uses: enzymes for the Krebs cycle or link reaction, proteins of the electron transport chain (such as A, B or C from part (b)), ATP synthase (D), and other membrane/transport/structural proteins. Some mitochondrial genes also code for the mitochondrion's own tRNA and rRNA, used to make its own ribosomes for translating these proteins.

reasoningChain: Recall what a mitochondrion needs to carry out respiration: enzymes, ETC proteins, ATP synthase, membrane proteins, and its own translation machinery (tRNA/rRNA).
List any three of these as suggested gene functions.

inferredMistakes.text: Suggesting generic cell functions unrelated to respiration (e.g. genes for cell division), rather than functions tied to what a mitochondrion itself does, since this is asking specifically about mitochondrial genes.
